stimulus.context: A film archive inspected reels from five collections. Two technicians share the restoration work; each is scheduled for 6 hours per day and spends 80% of that time actively restoring reels.

questions.stem: What percentage of the Documentary reels were usable?
questions.answer_reason: Usable percentage = 204 ÷ 240 × 100 = 85%. No rounding is required. The answer is 85%.

questions.stem: How many hours of restoration work are required for all usable Drama reels?
questions.answer_reason: The Drama collection has 162 usable reels. Work time = 162 × 22 = 3,564 minutes. Converting to hours gives 3,564 ÷ 60 = 59.4 hours. The answer is 59.4 hours.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of whole working days the two technicians need to restore all usable Science reels?
questions.answer_reason: Science restoration requires 114 × 18 = 2,052 minutes. The two technicians provide 2 × 6 × 60 × 0.80 = 576 active minutes per day. The work takes 2,052 ÷ 576 = 3.5625 days, so a fourth whole day is required. The answer is 4 days.

stimulus.context: A coastal laboratory processed water readings from four monitoring stations. Each positive reading requires a £6 confirmation test. The project also has a fixed setup cost of £450.

questions.stem: What percentage of the scheduled readings at East station were valid?
questions.answer_reason: Valid percentage = 184 ÷ 200 × 100 = 92%. The answer is 92%.

questions.stem: Across all four stations, what percentage of valid readings were positive, to the nearest 0.1%?
questions.answer_reason: Total positives = 37 + 46 + 51 + 21 = 155. Total valid readings = 148 + 184 + 153 + 126 = 611. The percentage is 155 ÷ 611 × 100 = 25.368...%, which rounds to 25.4%. The answer is 25.4%.

questions.stem: What was the total project cost, including processing, all confirmation tests and the fixed setup cost?
questions.answer_reason: Processing costs are 148 × £2.40 + 184 × £2.10 + 153 × £2.60 + 126 × £2.30 = £1,429.20. Confirmation tests cost 155 × £6 = £930. Adding the £450 setup cost gives £1,429.20 + £930 + £450 = £2,809.20. The answer is £2,809.20.

stimulus.context: An archaeological survey classified finds from five trenches as organic material or ceramic material. The bars show the number of finds in each category.

questions.stem: How many finds were recorded in Trench C altogether?
questions.answer_reason: Trench C contains 36 organic finds and 54 ceramic finds. Total = 36 + 54 = 90 finds. The answer is 90.

questions.stem: What percentage of the finds in Trench B were ceramic, to the nearest 0.1%?
questions.answer_reason: Trench B has 60 + 45 = 105 finds. The ceramic share is 45 ÷ 105 × 100 = 42.857...%, which rounds to 42.9%. The answer is 42.9%.

questions.stem: Across all five trenches, 15% of organic finds and 20% of ceramic finds are expected to need conservation. What is the estimated total number needing conservation, to the nearest whole find?
questions.answer_reason: There are 48 + 60 + 36 + 72 + 40 = 256 organic finds and 32 + 45 + 54 + 24 + 50 = 205 ceramic finds. Expected conservation work = 0.15 × 256 + 0.20 × 205 = 38.4 + 41 = 79.4 finds. Rounding the final total to the nearest whole find gives 79. The answer is 79.

stimulus.context: Two laser sensors were tested over six calibration cycles. The graph shows each sensor's absolute measurement deviation in micrometres (µm).

questions.stem: What was the difference between the two sensor deviations in Cycle 1?
questions.answer_reason: In Cycle 1, Sensor A deviated by 2 µm and Sensor B by 7 µm. The difference is 7 − 2 = 5 µm. The answer is 5 µm.

questions.stem: What was Sensor A's mean deviation across the six cycles, to the nearest 0.1 µm?
questions.answer_reason: Sensor A's deviations sum to 2 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 28 µm. Mean = 28 ÷ 6 = 4.666... µm, which rounds to 4.7 µm. The answer is 4.7 µm.

questions.stem: A technician spends 12 minutes correcting each micrometre by which a reading exceeds 4 µm. How much correction time is needed for all readings from both sensors?
questions.answer_reason: Sensor A exceeds 4 µm by 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 µm in total. Sensor B exceeds 4 µm by 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8 µm. Total excess = 15 µm, so correction time = 15 × 12 = 180 minutes = 3 hours. The answer is 3 hours.

stimulus.context: A conservation store contains 2,400 pottery fragments. The pie chart shows the number in each glaze category.

questions.stem: How many fragments have green glaze?
questions.answer_reason: Green glaze accounts for 22% of 2,400. The number is 0.22 × 2,400 = 528 fragments. The answer is 528.

questions.stem: How many more fragments have blue glaze than white glaze?
questions.answer_reason: The percentage-point difference is 30% − 15% = 15%. The number difference is 0.15 × 2,400 = 360 fragments. The answer is 360.

questions.stem: A further 120 unglazed fragments are added to the store. What percentage of the new total is unglazed, to the nearest 0.1%?
questions.answer_reason: Initially, 15% of 2,400 = 360 fragments are unglazed. After adding 120, there are 480 unglazed out of 2,520 total. The percentage is 480 ÷ 2,520 × 100 = 19.0476...%, which rounds to 19.0%. The answer is 19.0%.

stimulus.context: An observatory tested eight image exposures. Each labelled point shows exposure time and the number of faint objects detected in that image.

data.title: Exposure Time and Faint Objects Detected

questions.stem: How many objects were detected in the 35-minute exposure?
questions.answer_reason: The point with an exposure time of 35 minutes is F, whose y-value is 46 objects. The answer is 46.

questions.stem: Which labelled exposure detected the greatest number of objects per minute?
questions.answer_reason: Objects per minute are A: 18 ÷ 10 = 1.8; B: 24 ÷ 15 = 1.6; D: 35 ÷ 25 = 1.4; F: 46 ÷ 35 = 1.31; H: 55 ÷ 45 = 1.22. The greatest rate is 1.8 objects per minute at A. The answer is A.

questions.stem: Among exposures lasting at least 25 minutes, which also detected at least 1.3 objects per minute? What is the total number of objects detected by those qualifying exposures?
questions.answer_reason: For exposures of at least 25 minutes, the rates are D: 35 ÷ 25 = 1.40, E: 38 ÷ 30 = 1.27, F: 46 ÷ 35 = 1.31, G: 44 ÷ 40 = 1.10 and H: 55 ÷ 45 = 1.22 objects per minute. Only D and F meet at least 1.3, giving 35 + 46 = 81 objects. The answer is 81.

stimulus.context: An inspection drone can travel along the links shown. Edge labels give one-way flight times in minutes, and links can be used in either direction.

data.title: Drone Flight Times Between Inspection Points

questions.stem: How long is the direct flight from Buoy to Tower?
questions.answer_reason: The direct edge between Buoy and Tower is labelled 8 minutes. The answer is 8 minutes.

questions.stem: What is the shortest flight time from Base to Tower?
questions.answer_reason: Via Buoy, the time is 20 + 8 = 28 minutes. Via Reef, it is 14 + 16 = 30 minutes, and other routes are longer. The shortest flight time is 28 minutes.

questions.stem: The drone flies from Base to Rig by the quickest route, performs an inspection using 8 kWh, and returns to Base along the same route. Flying uses 0.6 kWh per minute. How much energy does the complete mission use?
questions.answer_reason: The quickest Base-to-Rig route is Base–Buoy–Cove–Rig: 20 + 12 + 11 = 43 minutes. A return along the same route makes 86 flight minutes. Flight energy = 86 × 0.6 = 51.6 kWh; adding 8 kWh for inspection gives 59.6 kWh. The answer is 59.6 kWh.

stimulus.context: The panel is a trapezium. Its parallel sides are 8 m and 12 m, its perpendicular height is 5 m, and each sloping side is 5.4 m.

questions.stem: What is the area of the panel?
questions.answer_reason: Area of a trapezium = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × perpendicular height. Therefore, area = ½ × (8 + 12) × 5 = 50 m². The answer is 50 m².

questions.stem: What is the perimeter of the panel?
questions.answer_reason: Perimeter = 8 + 12 + 5.4 + 5.4 = 30.8 m. The answer is 30.8 m.

questions.stem: A scale model uses a length scale of 1:25. What is the area of the model panel in cm²?
questions.answer_reason: The real area is 50 m² = 500,000 cm². A 1:25 length scale gives an area scale of 1:25² = 1:625. Model area = 500,000 ÷ 625 = 800 cm². The answer is 800 cm².

stimulus.text: A mapping drone must image a 54-hectare orchard. One battery covers 9 hectares during a 24-minute flight. Changing a battery takes 6 minutes between flights. Imaging produces 1.8 GB per hectare before compression; compression reduces the data to 40% of its original size. The upload connection transfers 12 GB per hour.

questions.stem: How many battery flights are required to image the whole orchard?
questions.answer_reason: Flights required = 54 hectares ÷ 9 hectares per flight = 6 flights. The answer is 6.

questions.stem: How long will the six flights and the battery changes between them take in total?
questions.answer_reason: Six flights take 6 × 24 = 144 minutes. There are five changes between six flights, taking 5 × 6 = 30 minutes. Total = 174 minutes = 2 hours 54 minutes. The answer is 2 hours 54 minutes.

questions.stem: How long will the compressed data take to upload, to the nearest minute?
questions.answer_reason: Original data = 54 × 1.8 = 97.2 GB. Compressed data = 97.2 × 0.40 = 38.88 GB. Upload time = 38.88 ÷ 12 = 3.24 hours = 3 hours 14.4 minutes, which rounds to 3 hours 14 minutes. The answer is 3 hours 14 minutes.

stimulus.text: A pottery studio makes a dry glaze mixture using 5 parts silica, 3 parts clay and 2 parts pigment by mass. A batch contains 36 kg of dry mixture. During preparation, 8% of the mixture is wasted. Each finished piece uses 0.69 kg of the remaining mixture. Silica costs £1.20 per kg, clay £0.80 per kg and pigment £3.50 per kg.

questions.stem: How much pigment is in the 36 kg dry batch?
questions.answer_reason: There are 5 + 3 + 2 = 10 total parts, of which 2 are pigment. Pigment mass = 36 × 2 ÷ 10 = 7.2 kg. The answer is 7.2 kg.

questions.stem: What is the maximum number of finished pieces that can be glazed after the 8% preparation waste?
questions.answer_reason: Remaining mixture = 36 × 0.92 = 33.12 kg. Number of pieces = 33.12 ÷ 0.69 = 48 exactly. The answer is 48 pieces.

questions.stem: What is the ingredient cost of the full 36 kg dry batch?
questions.answer_reason: The batch contains 18 kg silica, 10.8 kg clay and 7.2 kg pigment. Cost = 18 × £1.20 + 10.8 × £0.80 + 7.2 × £3.50 = £21.60 + £8.64 + £25.20 = £55.44. The answer is £55.44.

items.text: A carrier charges freight using the greater of each crate's actual mass and volumetric mass. The shipment also has one £42 handling fee.

items.context: Crate sizes, actual masses and quantities are shown below.

questions.stem: What billable mass is used for one Reagent pack crate?
questions.answer_reason: The volumetric mass is 50 × 40 × 30 ÷ 5,000 = 12 kg. This is greater than the 9.5 kg actual mass, so the billable mass is 12.0 kg. The answer is 12.0 kg.

questions.stem: What is the total billable mass of all 30 crates?
questions.answer_reason: Culture kits have volumetric mass 6 kg, so use actual mass: 12 × 7.2 = 86.4 kg. Reagent packs use volumetric mass: 8 × 12 = 96 kg. Sensor cases have volumetric mass 10.5 kg, so use actual mass: 10 × 11 = 110 kg. Total = 86.4 + 96 + 110 = 292.4 kg. The answer is 292.4 kg.

questions.stem: Freight costs £1.85 per billable kilogram. What is the total charge including the handling fee?
questions.answer_reason: The total billable mass is 292.4 kg. Freight costs 292.4 × £1.85 = £540.94. Adding the £42 handling fee gives £582.94. The answer is £582.94.

items.text: A radio telescope records data only during completed observing hours. An identical backup copy of all recorded data is required. Storage may be pooled across all purchased drives; original files and their backup copies do not need to occupy disjoint drives. Use 1 TB = 1,000 GB.
Completed hours = requested hours × completion percentage

items.context: The table summarises four fictional observing projects.

questions.stem: How many observing hours were completed for the Quasar project?
questions.answer_reason: Completed Quasar hours = 40 × 0.90 = 36 hours. The answer is 36 hours.

questions.stem: How many observing hours were completed across all four projects?
questions.answer_reason: Completed hours are Aurora 48 × 75% = 36, Pulsar 60 × 80% = 48, Quasar 40 × 90% = 36, and Galaxy 72 × 62.5% = 45. Total = 36 + 48 + 36 + 45 = 165 hours. The answer is 165 hours.

questions.stem: Assuming files may be distributed across all purchased drives and only their combined storage capacity matters, how many 2 TB drives are needed to hold all recorded data and one additional copy?
questions.answer_reason: Recorded data are Aurora 36 × 18 = 648 GB, Pulsar 48 × 15 = 720 GB, Quasar 36 × 24 = 864 GB, and Galaxy 45 × 12 = 540 GB. Total = 2,772 GB. Including an identical backup requires 5,544 GB. Each drive holds 2,000 GB, so 5,544 ÷ 2,000 = 2.772 and 3 whole drives are required. The answer is 3 drives.
